recipes.name: Mediterranean Greek Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 cup black olives, pitted and sliced
0.33333334326744 cup diced oil packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained, oil reserved

steps.text: In a large salad bowl, toss together the cucumbers, feta cheese, olives, roma tomatoes, sun-dried tomatoes, 2 tablespoons reserved sun-dried tomato oil, and red onion. Chill until serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Mediterranean Greek Salad
raw_recipe.description: Hearty, robust, and delicious! All the stuff you dreamed about in a Greek salad - tomatoes, olives, feta cheese, cucumbers, and sun-dried tomatoes - all glistening from a splash of oil.

review.reviewBody: Great, quick recipe, but I changed it a bit. I omitted the sun dried tomatoes, and just used olive oil, salt and freshly ground pepper for the dressing. I also chopped all ingredients for a nice texture and added fresh oregeno.

This salad is amazing. I made it for a side dish at a party we had and it was a HUGE hit :-) I used Kalamata olives instead of black, and did not use the reserved oil from the sun dried tomatoes, but rather the Absolutely Fabulous Greek/House Dressing recipe on this site. Wonderful stuff. I ended up chopping my cucumbers because I didn't have anything to slice them like in the picture. I think the ratio of all of the ingredients for the salad was perfect. This is now my go to Greek salad recipe.

The sun-dried tomatoes I had were not in oil, so I had to make a dressing. I just mixed some olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt and pepper for the dressing. I enjoyed this a lot as an alternative to a lettuce based salad. Next time I will try half black olives and half kalamata olives. This would also be good with a little orzo mixed in.

I was looking to make a different kind of Greek salad since I make one at least once a month in the summer as it is. However when I make mine, I use just plain vinegar. By adding red wine vinegar in this salad, it gave it a great tangy pop and I love the addition of the sun dried tomatoes. However, I still wanted to make it more Mediterranean, sort of like the med salads I have had in restaurants. So, keeping everything the same with the exception of the oil from the sun dried tomatoes (I used a good quality Greek olive oil instead) and adding a tbsp of red wine vinegar; I also used a heaping tbsp of Greek seasoning (an essential Greek spice in any kitchen) and I chopped up two romaine hearts lettuce. I mixed all the veggies, seasoning and lettuce together before I crumbled the feta on top. It was Out of this World. A great base recipe with a little pizzazz added is well worth the small effort to make this.

I made this for friends who limit their carb intake! This was delicious & fit the bill. I added a dressing made with fresh lemon juice & EVOO! I will make this again!
PS: I did not use the sun dried tomatoes!
Simple but good. I used pickled red onions and added finely julienned radish. A sure addition to our basics!

This was excellent. I'm unable to locate sun-dried tomatoes in my area so I subbed 1/3 cup sun-dried tomato pesto. I tossed the vegetables together, then added lemon juice, tossed them again, drizzled olive oil, and tossed once again. I used kalamata olives because I had them on hand.

This salad was really full of flavor. I added a few whole pepperonchini peppers for a little kick. For an afternoon lunch I added a few cubes of capicola ham and pepperoni and served it on top of crisp romain lettuce leaves. This is so flavorful and versatile. Just overall, a great recipe.

I love the ingredients and its a very simple salad that even a kid can make it. The oil from the sun dried tomatoes is not a powerful dressing, it needs some acidity and salt so I made a Vinaigrette with the oil from the tomatoes.

This is GREAT with some adjustments. I find that 3 cucumbers is too many; I use 2. And to make it more colorful, I peel the cucumber in stripes, leaving some of the skin on. For the dressing, I added 1/2 tsp oregano, 1 1/2 tsp lemon juice, 1 tsp red wine vinegar, and salt & pepper to taste. It's really a light & easy salad, and very tasty! Definitely use Kalamata olives, they make a world of difference. Make it, but just make it my way. :)

We lived in Namibia for a year and they served a lot of Greek and Mediterranean salads. This was a perfect reconstruction. I added sweet peppers from our garden. A great way to use our tomatoes and cucumbers from our CSA. I followed suggestion to add oregano and I used a bit more olive oil to supplement the sundried tomato oil. I also added a splash of balsamic vinegar and lemon juice. Wowsa. Excellent flavors.
Al I did was add some more of the sun dried tomatoes
I love the fresh Greek flavors of this salad

I enjoyed the combined ingredients in this recipe but the oil from the sundried tomato jar wasn't enough to give it the kick it seemed to need. I added some olive oil and balsamic vinegar and I think the vinegar made the whole thing a bit bitter. So I will have to find a recipe for Greek salad dressing the next time!

Turned out delicious! The next day I added 
lettuce to the mix.

Great dish. Dry light and bright. Perfect for summer. I served it over a bed of greens and paired it with a warm grain dish for a meatless dinner option. I decreased the tomatoes, olives, onions and cheese to my families tastes as well as omitting the oil from the sun dried tomatoes and using olive oil and balsamic to dress it.
